message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"31c23a6df08f0d88a332db1b534332350c266ec7ca6bdeb27fb4535e53443417","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mn-class-d:lineage:64","source_registry_sha256":"960e2daa314aff60b32f5124e42324d79615ce2a3ea953a336216b4593c0c910","units":[{"unit_id":"sec03-u01","module_id":"sec03-m01","objective_ids":["sec03-u01"],"title":{"text":"Who signs for a teen","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Every teen permit and license application needs an approved adult signature, and family situations change who that adult can be.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Mia is sixteen; her parents are divorced, she lives with her mother, and her stepfather offers to sign her permit application.","fact_ids":["sec03-F02"]},"reasoning":{"text":"When parents are divorced, the custodial parent or a stepparent married to the custodial parent may approve the application.","fact_ids":["sec03-F02"]},"result":{"text":"Mia's stepfather, married to her mother, may sign the application.","fact_ids":["sec03-F02"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a signature on a teen's application can never be taken back.","fact_ids":["sec03-F04"]},"correction":{"text":"The person who signed a teen's application may later withdraw that approval.","fact_ids":["sec03-F04"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Parent, guardian, foster parent or director signs, and the signer can take it back.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F04"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A married sixteen-year-old with no living parent wants a permit. Could their nineteen-year-old spouse sign?","fact_ids":["sec03-F03"]},"answer":{"text":"Yes; a spouse may sign if at least eighteen.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03"]},"rationale":{"text":"A teen with no living parent or guardian, or who is married or emancipated, may use a close relative, employer or spouse aged eighteen or older.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"The adult behind the application","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Teens need an approving adult","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05"]},{"text":"Who qualifies depends on family","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Every applicant under eighteen needs an adult to approve the permit or license application. This unit shows who that adult can be. You will start with the usual signers, then look at what happens when parents are divorced, when a teen has no living parent or guardian or is married or emancipated, and how foreign exchange students handle the signature. You will also learn that a signature is not final, because the person who signs can later change their mind. These rules matter at both the permit stage and the provisional license stage, so it is worth getting them straight now.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The usual signers","fact_ids":["sec03-F01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Parent","fact_ids":["sec03-F01"]},{"text":"Court-appointed guardian","fact_ids":["sec03-F01"]},{"text":"County foster parent or program director","fact_ids":["sec03-F01"]}],"narration":{"text":"An applicant under eighteen needs the permit or license application approved by one of four kinds of adult: a parent, a guardian appointed by a court, a foster parent appointed by a county, or the director of the transitional living program where the teen lives. If the signer is someone other than a parent, the documents showing that role come along to the office. Think of this list as closed. A favorite aunt, a coach or a family friend is not on it, unless the special rules for teens without parents apply, which you will see on the next slides.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Divorce and special situations","fact_ids":["sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Divorced: custodial parent or stepparent","fact_ids":["sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04"]},{"text":"No parent, married or emancipated","fact_ids":["sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04"]},{"text":"Signer must be at least eighteen","fact_ids":["sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04"]}],"narration":{"text":"When the parents are divorced, the custodial parent may approve the teen's application, and so may a stepparent who is married to the custodial parent. A teen who has no living parent or guardian, or who is married or legally emancipated, may instead have a close family member, an employer or a spouse sign, as long as that signer is at least eighteen. These options exist so that teens in less common family situations can still apply. Whoever signs takes on a real role, because the approval can later be withdrawn by the same person if they decide the teen is not ready.","fact_ids":["sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Exchange student signatures","fact_ids":["sec03-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Host sponsors need legal guardianship","fact_ids":["sec03-F05"]},{"text":"Otherwise two notarized parent forms","fact_ids":["sec03-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Foreign exchange students are a common source of confusion. It might seem natural for host sponsors to sign, since the student lives with them. But host sponsors may sign only if they have documented legal guardianship. Without it, the student brings two forms with the parents' notarized signatures: one for the instruction permit and one for the provisional license. That means planning ahead, because the forms have to come from the student's own parents and be notarized. If you are a host family, check whether you hold guardianship papers before assuming you can sign the application.","fact_ids":["sec03-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the spouse rule","fact_ids":["sec03-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Married sixteen-year-old","fact_ids":["sec03-F03"]},{"text":"No living parent; spouse is nineteen","fact_ids":["sec03-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a married sixteen-year-old has no living parent and wants an instruction permit. Could their nineteen-year-old spouse sign the application? Think about the special situations. A teen with no living parent or guardian, or who is married or legally emancipated, may have a close family member, an employer or a spouse sign, and that signer must be at least eighteen. The spouse is nineteen, so yes, the spouse may sign. If the spouse were only seventeen, a different eligible adult, such as a close family member or an employer aged eighteen or older, would need to sign instead.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Signer rules recap","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Parent, guardian, foster parent, director","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05"]},{"text":"Divorce: custodial parent or stepparent","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05"]},{"text":"Signer may withdraw approval","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"To sum up, a teen's application is approved by a parent, a court-appointed guardian, a county-appointed foster parent or the director of the teen's transitional living program. With divorced parents, the custodial parent or a stepparent married to that parent may sign. A teen with no living parent or guardian, or who is married or emancipated, may use a close relative, an employer or a spouse aged eighteen or older. Host sponsors sign only with documented guardianship; otherwise exchange students bring two notarized parent forms. And remember that the signer may later withdraw approval.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec03-u02","module_id":"sec03-m02","objective_ids":["sec03-u02"],"title":{"text":"The instruction permit","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-F07","sec03-F08"]},"why_how":[{"text":"The permit is where supervised practice begins, and its rules on supervisors, belts and phones differ for teens and adults.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F10","sec03-F11"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Noah is sixteen with a permit, and his licensed nineteen-year-old cousin offers to ride along while he practices.","fact_ids":["sec03-F10"]},"reasoning":{"text":"A permit holder under eighteen needs a supervising driver who is twenty-one or older, so the cousin does not qualify.","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-R01"]},"result":{"text":"Noah practices with his mother, who is over twenty-one, instead.","fact_ids":["sec03-F10"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a teen permit holder may use a hands-free phone while driving.","fact_ids":["sec03-F10"]},"correction":{"text":"A permit holder under eighteen may not use or talk on a cell phone at all, even hands-free.","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-R01"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Fifteen to start, supervisor twenty-one for teens, eighteen for adults, phone off.","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-F10","sec03-F11"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A twenty-year-old permit holder wants to practice with a licensed eighteen-year-old friend. Is that allowed?","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-R02"]},"answer":{"text":"Yes; adults eighteen or older may be supervised by a driver eighteen or older.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11"]},"rationale":{"text":"The twenty-one-year-old supervisor rule applies only to permit holders under eighteen.","fact_ids":["sec03-R02","sec03-F10"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Your learning license","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-F07","sec03-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"What the permit allows","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-F07","sec03-F08"]},{"text":"How to qualify","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-F07","sec03-F08"]},{"text":"Rules while practicing","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-F07","sec03-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"The instruction permit is the first stage of graduated driver licensing. It lets you practice on real roads with an experienced driver beside you. In this unit you will learn what the permit allows and how long it lasts, what it takes to qualify at fifteen or as an adult, the supervision, seat belt and phone rules for teens and for adults, how long you must hold it before the road test, and how to replace a lost or expired permit. The rules for drivers under eighteen are stricter, so pay attention to which age group each rule belongs to.","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-F07","sec03-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"What the permit allows","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F06","sec03-F13"]},"lines":[{"text":"Two years of supervised practice","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F06","sec03-F13"]},{"text":"Supervisor in the front passenger seat","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F06","sec03-F13"]},{"text":"Keep the permit with you","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F06","sec03-F13"]}],"narration":{"text":"An instruction permit covers two years of practice with a licensed supervising driver sitting in the front passenger seat. Practicing without a valid permit is illegal, and the permit must be with you whenever you drive. Under the Graduated Driver's Licensing system, a driver aged eighteen or younger must keep an instruction permit a minimum of six months before the road test. If your permit is lost or expires, you replace it by applying for a new one, which is valid for two years from the day you apply. Keep it in your wallet so it is never left at home.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F06","sec03-F13"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Qualifying for a permit","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-F09","sec03-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"At least fifteen","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-F09","sec03-R01"]},{"text":"Thirty classroom hours, or fifteen concurrent","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-F09","sec03-R01"]},{"text":"ID, vision, written test, application, fee","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-F09","sec03-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"To get a permit you must be at least fifteen years old. You must also either finish thirty hours of classroom instruction while enrolled in behind-the-wheel training, or be in a concurrent course with the first fifteen classroom hours done. If you are eighteen or older, no driver education is needed. Every applicant must meet the identification rules, pass the vision screening and the written test, complete an application and pay the permit fee. So a fifteen-year-old's path combines age, classroom progress and the same tests every new driver takes.","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-F09","sec03-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Teen permit rules","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Supervisor twenty-one or older","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-R01"]},{"text":"Everyone belted or in a child restraint","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-R01"]},{"text":"No cell phone, even hands-free","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"A permit holder under eighteen needs a supervising driver who is twenty-one or older. All occupants must wear a seat belt or ride in a child restraint, not just the driver. And the teen may not use or talk on a cell phone at all while driving, even with a hands-free device. Put together, the teen permit rules aim to give a new driver an experienced adult beside them, a buckled car and no phone distraction. A licensed sibling or friend under twenty-one cannot be the supervisor, however careful they are, so plan practice sessions around the adults in your life.","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Adult permit rules","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Supervisor eighteen or older","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-R02"]},{"text":"Everyone belted","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-R02"]},{"text":"Road test after three months at nineteen","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Permit holders aged eighteen or older follow lighter rules. They may be supervised by a driver aged eighteen or older, and everyone in the vehicle must still wear a seat belt or ride in a child restraint. The road test may be taken after six months of practice driving, or after three months for a permit holder aged nineteen or older. So the adult supervisor age drops from twenty-one to eighteen, and the waiting time drops from six months to three, but only once the permit holder is nineteen. An eighteen-year-old still waits the full six months.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s6","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Phones and supervisor ages","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-R01","sec03-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Teen: no phone at all","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-R01","sec03-R02"]},{"text":"Teen supervisor twenty-one, adult eighteen","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-R01","sec03-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Two details trip people up. First, some teens believe a hands-free phone call is fine with a supervisor beside them. It is not. A permit holder under eighteen may not use or talk on a cell phone, even hands-free. Second, people mix up the supervisor ages. A teen's supervisor must be twenty-one or older, while an adult permit holder's supervisor need only be eighteen or older. When a question describes a permit holder, check their age first. That single fact decides the supervisor age, the phone rule and whether the road test can come after three months or six.","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-R01","sec03-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s7","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check an adult supervisor","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-R02","sec03-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Permit holder is twenty","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-R02","sec03-F10"]},{"text":"Supervisor is eighteen","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-R02","sec03-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a twenty-year-old permit holder wants to practice with a licensed eighteen-year-old friend. Is that allowed? Think about which rules apply. A permit holder aged eighteen or older may be supervised by a driver aged eighteen or older, as long as everyone is belted or in a child restraint. The twenty-one-or-older supervisor rule only applies to permit holders under eighteen. So yes, the eighteen-year-old friend can supervise. If the permit holder were seventeen, the same friend would be too young, and a supervisor aged twenty-one or older would be required.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-R02","sec03-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s8","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Permit rules recap","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F09","sec03-F10","sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-F13","sec03-R01","sec03-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Fifteen plus classroom hours to start","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F09","sec03-F10","sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-F13","sec03-R01","sec03-R02"]},{"text":"Teens: twenty-one supervisor, no phone","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F09","sec03-F10","sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-F13","sec03-R01","sec03-R02"]},{"text":"Six months, or three at nineteen","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F09","sec03-F10","sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-F13","sec03-R01","sec03-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"To wrap up, a permit allows two years of practice with a licensed supervisor in the front passenger seat, must be with you whenever you drive, and is replaced by applying for a new one valid two years. You qualify at fifteen with thirty classroom hours or fifteen hours of a concurrent course, or at eighteen with no driver education, plus identification, vision and written tests and a fee. Teens need a supervisor twenty-one or older, belts for all and no phone at all, while adults need a supervisor eighteen or older. The road test follows six months of practice, or three months at nineteen or older.","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F09","sec03-F10","sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-F13","sec03-R01","sec03-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec03-u03","module_id":"sec03-m03","objective_ids":["sec03-u03"],"title":{"text":"The provisional license","fact_ids":["sec03-F14","sec03-F15","sec03-F16"]},"why_how":[{"text":"The provisional license is a teen's first chance to drive alone, and its limits on nights and passengers protect new drivers in their riskiest months.","fact_ids":["sec03-F14","sec03-F18","sec03-F19"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Ella got her provisional license four months ago and wants to drive three friends, all under twenty, to a game with no parent along.","fact_ids":["sec03-F19"]},"reasoning":{"text":"In the first six months a provisional driver may carry only one passenger under twenty unless a parent or guardian is in the vehicle.","fact_ids":["sec03-F19","sec03-R05"]},"result":{"text":"Ella takes one friend, or asks a parent to come along so all three can ride.","fact_ids":["sec03-F19","sec03-R05"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking any licensed adult riding along lifts the provisional night limit.","fact_ids":["sec03-R04"]},"correction":{"text":"Only a licensed driver at least twenty-five years old lifts the midnight to five limit, apart from the work, school event and employment exceptions.","fact_ids":["sec03-R04","sec03-F18"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Midnight to five off, one then three passengers, forty or fifty logged hours.","fact_ids":["sec03-F18","sec03-R05","sec03-F16"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A provisional driver in month two is driving home from work at one in the morning, alone. Is this allowed?","fact_ids":["sec03-F18"]},"answer":{"text":"Yes; driving between home and work is an exception to the night limit.","fact_ids":["sec03-F18"]},"rationale":{"text":"The night limit has exceptions for a companion twenty-five or older, home to work or school event trips, and employment.","fact_ids":["sec03-F18","sec03-R04"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Driving solo with limits","fact_ids":["sec03-F14","sec03-F15","sec03-F18"]},"lines":[{"text":"Second stage of graduated licensing","fact_ids":["sec03-F14","sec03-F15","sec03-F18"]},{"text":"Eligibility, night and passenger rules","fact_ids":["sec03-F14","sec03-F15","sec03-F18"]}],"narration":{"text":"The provisional license is the second stage of graduated licensing, and for most teens it is the first time they drive without a supervisor. It comes with rules designed for the first year of solo driving. In this unit you will learn how long it lasts, who qualifies, how many supervised hours must be logged, the road test and signature requirements, the night driving limit and its exceptions, and the passenger caps that change after six months. The numbers here are among the most tested in the whole manual, so read each slide with care.","fact_ids":["sec03-F14","sec03-F15","sec03-F18"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Provisional license basics","fact_ids":["sec03-F14","sec03-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Valid two years from application","fact_ids":["sec03-F14","sec03-R03"]},{"text":"Everyone belted","fact_ids":["sec03-F14","sec03-R03"]},{"text":"No cell phone, even hands-free","fact_ids":["sec03-F14","sec03-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"The provisional license is valid for two years from the application date. Every occupant must be belted, and cell phone use is banned for the driver, hands-free included. Both the instruction permit and the provisional license run for two years, but the permit counts from the day you apply for it and the provisional license from its own application date. So the two-year clock restarts when you move up. Keep the phone rule in mind, too. It carries over unchanged from the permit stage, which means a provisional driver may not make or take calls while driving, even through the car's speakers.","fact_ids":["sec03-F14","sec03-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Who qualifies","fact_ids":["sec03-F15","sec03-F17"]},"lines":[{"text":"At least sixteen","fact_ids":["sec03-F15","sec03-F17"]},{"text":"Both driver education phases","fact_ids":["sec03-F15","sec03-F17"]},{"text":"Six clean months with a permit","fact_ids":["sec03-F15","sec03-F17"]}],"narration":{"text":"To get a provisional license you must be at least sixteen, have finished both the classroom and behind-the-wheel phases of driver education, and have held a permit for six months with no moving, alcohol or controlled substance convictions. You must also pass the road test and have an application signed by an approved adult such as a parent or guardian. Each requirement stands on its own. Turning sixteen is not enough if the six months are not up, and six months is not enough if a moving violation conviction happened along the way. Treat your permit months as part of the qualification.","fact_ids":["sec03-F15","sec03-F17"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The supervised driving log","fact_ids":["sec03-F16"]},"lines":[{"text":"Forty hours with the parent class","fact_ids":["sec03-F16"]},{"text":"Fifty hours without it","fact_ids":["sec03-F16"]},{"text":"Fifteen at night either way","fact_ids":["sec03-F16"]}],"narration":{"text":"The supervised driving log must show a set number of hours. If a parent takes the class from an approved driver education program, the log needs at least forty hours, including fifteen at night. Without that parent class, the log needs at least fifty hours, including fifteen at night. In other words, the parent class trades ten hours of logged practice, while the night hours stay the same at fifteen. Fill the log as you go rather than trying to reconstruct it at the end, and make sure each night session is recorded as night driving so the fifteen hours add up correctly.","fact_ids":["sec03-F16"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"The night limit","fact_ids":["sec03-F18","sec03-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"First six months","fact_ids":["sec03-F18","sec03-R04"]},{"text":"No driving midnight to five","fact_ids":["sec03-F18","sec03-R04"]},{"text":"Three exceptions","fact_ids":["sec03-F18","sec03-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"In the first six months, a provisional driver may not drive between midnight and five in the morning. There are three exceptions. The driver may drive in those hours with a licensed driver who is at least twenty-five years old, when driving between home and work or a school event without school transportation, or when driving for employment. The age of that companion is the detail people forget. A licensed friend who is twenty-two does not lift the limit; the companion must be at least twenty-five. After the first six months, this particular night limit no longer applies.","fact_ids":["sec03-F18","sec03-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s6","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Passenger caps","fact_ids":["sec03-F19","sec03-F20","sec03-F21","sec03-R05"]},"lines":[{"text":"First six months: one under twenty","fact_ids":["sec03-F19","sec03-F20","sec03-F21","sec03-R05"]},{"text":"Second six months: up to three","fact_ids":["sec03-F19","sec03-F20","sec03-F21","sec03-R05"]},{"text":"Parent aboard or family lifts it","fact_ids":["sec03-F19","sec03-F20","sec03-F21","sec03-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Passenger limits also change over the first year. In the first six months, a provisional driver may carry only one passenger under twenty unless a parent or guardian is in the vehicle.
